prospect.name: Mario Gallegos
prospect.location: Downtown Los Angeles, California, USA. Born in Mexico City.
prospect.occupation: Los Angeles Unified School District — oversees maintenance of the headquarters building. Three to four years from retirement. Started working at fourteen to help provide for his family; oldest of four boys.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife retires about four years after him and he has just bought her her first pair of hiking boots. Three children — a 27-year-old daughter, a 22-year-old daughter and a 19-year-old son. Practising Catholic with a one-to-one session booked with his priest the following day. Currently in the process of buying a house.
prospect.training_background: Never played sports and describes himself as having never been in shape. Hikes a minimum of seven miles a week, usually at the weekend, plus some cycling; summited Mount Whitney last year at 14,505 ft. Was over 200 lb last September and is 175 now. Has done CrossFit previously — lost weight but it 'was tearing up my body'. Recently following Trevor's content and attempting the movements: about 120 push-ups across sets three times a week, 10 pull-ups in small sets three times a week, and about 120 halos with a 30 lb kettlebell. Has stopped all of it in the last two weeks.
prospect.medical: A fifteen-year cycle of recurrent injury that stops every training attempt at the four-to-five-month mark. CURRENTLY: tennis elbow described as 'really bad'; right shoulder pain preventing push-ups; right hip pain. Sciatic nerve injury from going up in weight on Trevor's movements, resolved only about three weeks before the call. Cannot perform a burpee — 'that'll trigger my sciatic nerve'. Back injury from moving boxes incorrectly in his early twenties, never treated. About a year ago described himself as 'a walking time bomb for a heart attack' with raised blood pressure at over 200 lb. Eats a carnivore-leaning diet of roughly two pounds of meat a day and has been fasting 22 hours daily since February, eating twice a day at weekends. No current medications disclosed, and none were asked about. No clinician has been consulted about any of the current injuries and no clearance was sought on this call.

signals: The defining obstacle is a fifteen-year injury pattern that has blocked every attempt: 'I get started, I'm doing good, I go four or five months, I'm doing really good, and then I get injured, something happens, and then I gotta stop'
Currently unable to perform basic programme movements — no burpees because of the sciatic nerve, no push-ups because of the right shoulder, and he has stopped pull-ups and halos entirely
Extremely high intent, which is the archetype's other marker: rated his need for the programme a 10 out of 10 and answered the readiness challenge with 'Let's do it'

PARTIAL MISMATCH: the archetype specifies no price resistance, and here price is a live constraint — a household rule requiring discussion above $1,000, a house purchase in progress and a history of serious debt. Confidence is held down accordingly.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED: the_preserver fits on age, low discretionary liquidity and the golden-years framing, but he is not already medically managed — his injuries are untreated — and he is chasing gains rather than holding function. the_rebuilder was rejected because there is no former self: 'I've always wanted to be in shape. Never was in shape. I never played sports.'

goals.text: Walk the Camino de Santiago the day after he retires — the one big item on his bucket list
Live his golden years as healthy as possible and enjoy retirement
See how close he can get to 100 years of age, with quality of life
Break the fifteen-year cycle of getting injured every time he starts training
Keep hiking and get his wife hiking with him — he has just bought her her first boots
Be able to keep working with his hands and doing things around the house
Lose the remaining weight — 'I'm still overweight, I totally have a dad bod'
Make the second half of his life better than the first
Model consistency for his three children, whom he tells to stay fit and watch their technique

pains.text: Fifteen-year cycle of injury that resets every attempt at four to five months — 'it's just this vicious cycle of doing the same thing over and over, and I can never get to my end goal'
Active tennis elbow described as really bad, which stopped his kettlebell work
Sciatic nerve injury from progressing weight too fast on Trevor's movements, only resolved three weeks before the call
Right shoulder pain that has stopped push-ups, halos and pull-ups within the last two weeks
Right hip pain, and an untreated back injury from his early twenties
Carries all of it entirely alone — 'All my aches and pains, my issues, they're all internalized, just me, myself, and I, and the man upstairs'
Discouraged and frustrated by the pattern, for the best part of two decades
Has become comfortable with chronic pain — 'they've been with me, they're almost like, I don't want to say my BFFs'
Pushes too hard too fast and cannot self-regulate load — 'Maybe I wanted the results faster than what it should be. I went up in weight... and then I hurt my sciatic nerve'
Was a year ago, by his own description, 'a walking time bomb for a heart attack' with raised blood pressure at over 200 lb
Never played sports, started work at fourteen to support the family, and has never been in shape in his life
Work stress at LAUSD, with a visible eye twitch he attributes to it

objections.raw_quote: Before I spend any type of money like that, my wife and I have this thing where we talk about it before... we've always stuck to the basic rules of like, hey, we said it's limit of anything over a thousand dollars. We need to talk about it before.
objections.rep_response: Ran the permission-versus-input distinction — 'is it just a situation where you're letting her know... or is it asking, hey honey, do you think I should do this?' — then played devil's advocate on a refusal, then proposed the $1,200 one-month trial as a way to bring the wife into the Trevor call and let her see what she is buying

objections.raw_quote: The other part could be financial, you know... Because we are also in the process of buying a house.
objections.rep_response: Did not explore it. No financial-picture questions were run at any point; the rep addressed it only later by moving to a cheaper tier

objections.raw_quote: But my hesitation is, will I be able to do it with, you know, my little injuries here and there? Will I be able to? Because I've also tried CrossFit... it was tearing up my body. I just could not keep up. Right now, to be honest, if you tell me, do a burpee, I can't. That'll trigger my sciatic nerve.
objections.rep_response: 'That's why we don't design anything until we've done an audit of your body and what you're currently capable of... Remember, this is not a rushed process for that reason that you just said'

objections.raw_quote: they did pretty much that when I was doing CrossFit. They developed a meal plan for me, I followed the meal plan, I went in, did their exercises, and then the accountability was there, because if I don't go to class, they're going to call me and say, where are you at?
objections.rep_response: Did not differentiate. Accepted it as evidence that the model works for him and moved on

objections.raw_quote: we are also in the process of buying a house... We're hoping to do that this year. So things are going into play. So, you know, that's going to take a little bit of that portion.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it and used it to justify the trial as a smaller commitment — 'doesn't take too much off the table for you guys, as you said you're investing into the house'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Referenced only — 'Most people tend to pop it on a credit card, but we have different in-house payment plan options if necessary.' Nothing was structured, and no plan was offered even after a household $1,000 decision threshold was disclosed.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: On the trial: 'If it's actually working for you... we can discuss extending you to the six or the 12. If not, we can shake hands and part ways as friends. If it's not financially feasible at that time, again, we can part ways at that point.' Plus the differential upgrade mechanic. Also a therapeutic claim during pillar one: 'any pains that you're experiencing are naturally going to be subsided.'

evidence: No payment, no link sent and no agreement. The prospect asked for an hour to speak to his wife: 'Can I let you know in an hour?'
Strongly positive lean: 'Give me about an hour and I will text you back with a yes, which I'm leaning towards' and again 'Give me about an hour and I'll text you with an answer for sure.'
The commitment work landed cleanly before price — need rated 10 out of 10, and the capability check answered 'Yes' to 'do you feel internally capable of getting out of this cycle of injuries?'
Target is the $1,200 one-month trial, which the rep recommended after the spouse objection surfaced; the prospect had been leaning toward the twelve-month tier before price was quoted
COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the household rule requires joint discussion above $1,000 and the trial is $1,200, so it does not actually clear the threshold that produced the objection
COUNTER-EVIDENCE: a house purchase is in progress and the prospect anticipates the conversation going badly — 'She's gonna go through the roof. She's like, are you giving $6,000 for you?'
outcome.next_step: Prospect to speak with his wife and text the rep's personal UK mobile within roughly an hour with a decision on the $1,200 one-month trial

notable.note: The highest-intent and lowest-ICP-fit prospect in the batch, and the one with the most active injuries. A 58-year-old with current tennis elbow, right shoulder pain that has stopped him doing push-ups, right hip pain, sciatica resolved only three weeks earlier, and a fifteen-year documented pattern of injuring himself every single time he trains — who states plainly that he cannot perform a burpee — was moved toward a loaded kettlebell programme with no clinician mentioned, no clearance sought and no suggestion that anyone medical look at him. His last injury was caused by attempting Trevor's own movements and progressing the weight. The rep answered the safety question with the baseline audit and asserted during pillar one that 'any pains that you're experiencing are naturally going to be subsided.' Two secondary items: the rep endorsed 22-hour daily fasting and called it 'the biggest correlator between longevity' to a man in his fifties recovering from repeated soft-tissue injury on two pounds of meat a day; and having heard that the household requires joint discussion on anything above $1,000, he proposed a $1,200 trial and encouraged a same-day text to the wife rather than the conversation the rule describes. Set against that, the emotional discovery in the first fifteen minutes — drawing out that this man has carried chronic pain for fifteen years without telling a single person — is the best work in this folder.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion throughout, including long stretches where the rep's pillar delivery sits under the prospect's label. Clear examples: 'There are only three pillars to this entire system' at 00:20:49 is labelled mario.gallegos and is the rep; 'Okay, you said no very quickly. Why not?' at 00:06:34 is split across both labels; 'And what you say for yourself there, Mario, is time' at 00:27:24 is labelled mario.gallegos and is the rep addressing him by name. The prospect appears under a work email handle rather than a name, and his name is recovered from the file title. The rep's own dog interrupts at 00:27:24 ('Zeke, stop!'), which is unrelated to the prospect's family. One artefact renders 'BFFs' as 'VFFs' at 00:18:00. Roles resolved from content throughout.
